question: Why did Pollan end his book by hunting, gathering and cooking one meal himself?
answer: To know exactly where every part of a meal came from. He shot a wild pig, foraged mushrooms and gathered sea salt, and found the meal slow and costly, no model for daily life. Its value, he argued, was the awareness: seeing the full cost of food, including the taking of a life.
move: Knowing the full cost of something changes how you value it.
simply: Pollan cooked one meal from scratch: he shot the pig, picked the mushrooms, even gathered the salt. It showed him how much hides behind any meal.
why: You don't need to hunt, but tracing one meal back to its sources, even in thought, makes food choices more conscious.
